from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Base class for maintaining layout and positioning consistency
class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Teaching Scene Setup
        lecture_lines_text = [
            "Numbers alone cannot describe a world in motion.",
            "We need a way to capture how things change.",
            "Differential equations are rules for this growth."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: Capturing Movement", lecture_lines_text)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Description: Create a [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] silhouette and a ground line. [Color: #FFFF00]
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Ground line along the F row
        ground = Line(self.grid["F1"] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid["F6"] + RIGHT*0.5, color=GREY_B)
        
        # Cheetah SVG asset placed above ground (E row)
        cheetah = SVGMobject("/mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg")
        cheetah.set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(cheetah, "E1", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(ground), FadeIn(cheetah))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Description: Move the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] across with increasing speed and a velocity vector. [Color: #00FF00]
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Velocity arrow setup
        vel_arrow = Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color="#00FF00", buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        vel_arrow.set_width(0.01) # Start small (at rest)
        
        # Tracker for progress 0 to 1
        tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        start_pos = self.grid["E1"]
        end_pos = self.grid["E6"]
        
        def cheetah_updater(mob):
            t = tracker.get_value()
            # Quadratic position for acceleration: p(t) = start + (end-start)*t^2
            mob.move_to(start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (t**2))

        def arrow_updater(mob):
            t = tracker.get_value()
            current_cheetah_pos = start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (t**2)
            mob.move_to(current_cheetah_pos + UP * 0.5, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            # Velocity is derivative of t^2 -> 2t. Scale arrow width by tracker.
            new_width = max(0.01, t * 2.0)
            mob.set_width(new_width, stretch=True, about_edge=LEFT)

        cheetah.add_updater(cheetah_updater)
        vel_arrow.add_updater(arrow_updater)
        
        self.add(vel_arrow)
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        cheetah.clear_updaters()
        vel_arrow.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Description: Display text 'Rate of Change' and link it to the acceleration of the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg]. [Color: #FFFFFF]
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Labels and formulas using the Visual Anchor System
        roc_text = Text("Rate of Change", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(roc_text, "A3")
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{dv}{dt} = a", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.3)
        
        # Acceleration label near the cheetah's end position
        accel_label = Text("Acceleration", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(accel_label, "D5")

        # Visual links
        link_1 = Arrow(self.grid["A3"] + DOWN * 0.3, self.grid["B3"] + UP * 0.3, color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        link_2 = Arrow(self.grid["B3"] + DOWN * 0.4, self.grid["D5"] + UP * 0.3, color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(roc_text))
        self.play(Create(link_1), FadeIn(formula))
        self.play(Create(link_2), FadeIn(accel_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with specific title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Bridge: The Slope as a Rate", 
            [
                'The derivative represents the slope at a point.', 
                'It tells us our instantaneous rate of change.', 
                'Knowing every slope allows us to reconstruct paths.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Color constants from instruction
        COLOR_CURVE = "#888888"
        COLOR_TANGENT = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_VALUE = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE))
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 9, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color=COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        point_tracker = ValueTracker(1.5)
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            val = point_tracker.get_value()
            # Map val in [-3, 3] to alpha in [0, 1] for TangentLine
            alpha = (val + 3) / 6
            return TangentLine(curve, alpha=alpha, length=3, color=COLOR_TANGENT)
        
        def get_dot():
            val = point_tracker.get_value()
            return Dot(axes.c2p(val, val**2), color=COLOR_VALUE)

        tangent = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        dot = always_redraw(get_dot)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(dot), Create(tangent))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_TANGENT))
        self.play(point_tracker.animate.set_value(-1.5), run_time=2)
        self.play(point_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_VALUE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize standard layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'An ODE relates a function to its derivatives.',
            'We solve for functions, not just single numbers.',
            'This equation locks the value and slope together.',
            'For example, growth increases as the value rises.',
            "The function's behavior depends on its current state."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the ODE: The Puzzle", lecture_lines)

        # Colors based on prompt
        COLOR_EQ = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_SEGMENT = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_FIELD = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_CURVE = "#FFA500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Using Text and VGroup to avoid LaTeX dependency (MathTex)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_EQ)
        equation = VGroup(
            Text("dy/dx"), 
            Text("="), 
            Text("y")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).set_color(COLOR_EQ)
        
        # Position in top half of right side
        self.place_in_area(equation, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        y_var = equation[2]
        label_y = Text("unknown function", font_size=18, color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        label_y.next_to(y_var, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        glow_box = SurroundingRectangle(y_var, color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(glow_box), Create(label_y))
        # Pulsating effect
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(y_var.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.4)
            self.play(y_var.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_SEGMENT)
        
        # Transitioning to graph view: Fade equation parts
        self.play(FadeOut(equation), FadeOut(label_y), FadeOut(glow_box))
        
        # Coordinate system on the grid area C1:F6
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.2,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_B}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "C1", "F6")
        self.play(Create(axes))
        
        # Point (0, 1) has y=1, so slope = 1
        p_scene = axes.c2p(0, 1)
        angle = np.arctan(1)
        length = 0.5
        dx = length * np.cos(angle)
        dy = length * np.sin(angle)
        
        segment = Line(
            p_scene - np.array([dx, dy, 0]),
            p_scene + np.array([dx, dy, 0]),
            color=COLOR_SEGMENT,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        dot = Dot(p_scene, color=COLOR_SEGMENT, radius=0.06)
        seg_label = Text("slope = y", font_size=20, color=COLOR_SEGMENT)
        seg_label.next_to(segment, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(dot), Create(segment), Write(seg_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_FIELD)
        
        # Construct slope field manually
        field = VGroup()
        x_pts = np.arange(-1.5, 1.6, 0.75)
        y_pts = np.arange(0.5, 3.6, 0.75)
        for x in x_pts:
            for y in y_pts:
                slope = y
                ang = np.arctan(slope)
                v_len = 0.2
                dx_v = v_len * np.cos(ang)
                dy_v = v_len * np.sin(ang)
                mid = axes.c2p(x, y)
                s = Line(
                    mid - np.array([dx_v, dy_v, 0]),
                    mid + np.array([dx_v, dy_v, 0]),
                    color=COLOR_FIELD,
                    stroke_width=2
                )
                field.add(s)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(seg_label), FadeOut(segment), FadeOut(dot))
        self.play(Create(field))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Curve y = exp(x)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(x), x_range=[-2, 1.3], color=COLOR_CURVE)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout with script lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "We can visualize solutions using a slope field.",
            "Every point shows a tiny arrow of direction.",
            "These arrows map the required slope everywhere.",
            "A solution is a path following these arrows.",
            "Like a boat drifting along a river's current."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Solutions: Slope Fields", lecture_lines)

        # Coordinate system for the slope field
        # Positioned in the A1-F6 grid area
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            y_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_B, "stroke_width": 2},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')

        # ODE: dy/dx = y / 2
        def get_slope_line(x_val, y_val, length=0.25, color="#555555"):
            slope = y_val / 2
            angle = np.arctan(slope)
            p1 = axes.c2p(x_val - (length/2) * np.cos(angle), y_val - (length/2) * np.sin(angle))
            p2 = axes.c2p(x_val + (length/2) * np.cos(angle), y_val + (length/2) * np.sin(angle))
            return Line(p1, p2, color=color, stroke_width=2)

        slope_field = VGroup()
        for x in np.arange(-2.0, 2.1, 0.5):
            for y in np.arange(-2.0, 2.1, 0.5):
                slope_field.add(get_slope_line(x, y))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color: #555555 (Grey) for the field
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#555555"))
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(slope_field, lag_ratio=0.05), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight individual arrows to show "tiny arrow of direction"
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#555555"))
        highlight_arrows = VGroup(*[slope_field[i] for i in [42, 43, 44, 45]])
        self.play(highlight_arrows.animate.set_color(YELLOW).scale(1.5), run_time=1)
        self.play(highlight_arrows.animate.set_color("#555555").scale(1/1.5), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#555555"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Tracing a single solution curve: y = e^(x/2)
        # Color: #0000FF (Blue)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        
        curve_func = lambda x: np.exp(x/2)
        solution_path = axes.plot(curve_func, x_range=[-2.5, 1.8], color="#0000FF", stroke_width=4)
        
        start_point = axes.c2p(-2.5, curve_func(-2.5))
        boat_dot = Dot(start_point, color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        # Use a simple dot to represent the "boat"
        
        self.add(boat_dot)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(boat_dot, solution_path), Create(solution_path), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Showing a family of curves: y = C * e^(x/2)
        # Color: #FFFFFF (White)
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        family = VGroup()
        c_values = [-1.5, -0.7, 0.3, 1.5]
        for c in c_values:
            curve = axes.plot(lambda x, c_val=c: c_val * np.exp(x/2), x_range=[-2.5, 2.2 if c <= 1 else 1.2], color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.6)
            family.add(curve)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(family, lag_ratio=0.3), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Define colors

        ).add_coordinates()

        # Labels for the axes using Text
        x_axis_label = Text("t (time)", font_size=20).next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), DOWN)
        y_axis_label = Text("P (population)", font_size=20).next_to(axes.y_axis.get_end(), LEFT).rotate(90 * DEGREES).shift(UP * 0.5)

        # Equations using Text to ensure maximum compatibility across environments
        ode_equation = Text("dP/dt = kP", color=color_ode, font_size=32)
        ode_equation.to_corner(UL, buff=0.5)

        solution_equation = Text("P(t) = P0 * e^(kt)", color=color_sol, font_size=28)
        solution_equation.next_to(ode_equation, DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)

        # Growth model constants
        p_zero = 10
        growth_rate = 0.6

        # Growth curve definition: P(t) = 10 * e^(0.6t)
        growth_curve = axes.plot(
            lambda t: p_zero * np.exp(growth_rate * t),
            x_range=[0, 3.8],
            color=color_curve,
            stroke_width=4
        )

        curve_label = Text("Exponential Growth", font_size=20, color=color_curve)
        curve_label.next_to(growth_curve.points[-1], UR, buff=0.2)

        # --- Animation Sequence ---
        
        # 1. Create coordinate system
        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Write(x_axis_label), Write(y_axis_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # 2. Show the Differential Equation
        self.play(Write(ode_equation))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 3. Show the Analytical Solution
        self.play(Write(solution_equation))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Animate the growth curve creation
        self.play(
            Create(growth_curve),
            Write(curve_label),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Highlight a specific point on the curve
        t_snapshot = 2.5
        p_snapshot = p_zero * np.exp(growth_rate * t_snapshot)
        point_coords = axes.c2p(t_snapshot, p_snapshot)
        
        target_dot = Dot(point_coords, color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        projection_lines = axes.get_lines_to_point(point_coords)
        
        snapshot_label = Text(f"P({t_snapshot}) ≈ {int(p_snapshot)}", font_size=18)
        snapshot_label.next_to(target_dot, UL, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(projection_lines), FadeIn(target_dot, scale=0.5))
        self.play(Write(snapshot_label))
        
        self.wait(3)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lines
        lines = [
            'One equation can have many possible solutions.',
            'An initial condition picks one unique path.',
            'This specific path is the particular solution.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("General vs. Particular Solutions", lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_GENERAL = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_POINT = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_PARTICULAR = "#FFD700"

        # Create Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 5, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_C},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")

        # Family of curves: y = e^x + C
        # We'll use C values: -1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0
        # The point (0, 2) corresponds to 2 = e^0 + C => C = 1
        c_values = [-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0]
        curves = VGroup()
        particular_curve_index = 3 # index of C=1.0

        for c in c_values:
            curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(x) + c, x_range=[-2, 1.4], color=COLOR_GENERAL)
            curves.add(curve)

        # Label for General Solution - Replaced MathTex with Text
        general_label = Text("y = e^x + C", color=COLOR_GENERAL, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(general_label, "A3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_GENERAL))
        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(curves), Write(general_label), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight initial condition (0, 2)
        dot = Dot(axes.coords_to_point(0, 2), color=COLOR_POINT)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text
        dot_label = Text("(0, 2)", color=COLOR_POINT, font_size=24)
        dot_label.next_to(dot, UR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_POINT))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(dot_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out non-particular curves and change the chosen one to GOLD
        particular_curve = curves[particular_curve_index]
        other_curves = VGroup(*[curves[i] for i in range(len(curves)) if i != particular_curve_index])
        
        particular_solution_label = Text("Particular Solution", color=COLOR_PARTICULAR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(particular_solution_label, "E3")
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text
        particular_formula = Text("y = e^x + 1", color=COLOR_PARTICULAR, font_size=36)
        particular_formula.set_stroke(width=1) # Visual bolding
        self.place_at_grid(particular_formula, "F3")

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_PARTICULAR))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(other_curves),
            FadeOut(general_label),
            particular_curve.animate.set_color(COLOR_PARTICULAR).set_stroke(width=6),
            FadeIn(particular_solution_label),
            FadeIn(particular_formula)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout
        lines = [
            'ODEs govern everything from orbits to cooling coffee.',
            'They bridge physical laws and future predictions.',
            'Master this language to understand the world.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Real-World Scope", lines)
        
        # Internal time tracker for updaters
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        self.add(time_tracker)
        time_tracker.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.increment_value(dt))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line and show orbit visual
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        orbit_center = self.grid["C4"]
        sun = Dot(point=orbit_center, color=YELLOW, radius=0.2)
        planet = Dot(point=orbit_center + RIGHT * 1.2, color=BLUE, radius=0.1)
        orbit_path = Circle(radius=1.2, color=GREY_A, stroke_width=1).move_to(orbit_center)
        
        planet.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            orbit_center + np.array([
                1.2 * np.cos(time_tracker.get_value() * 2),
                1.2 * np.sin(time_tracker.get_value() * 2),
                0
            ])
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(orbit_path), FadeIn(sun), FadeIn(planet))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Visual for bridge/prediction
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["E2"], end=self.grid["E6"], color=BLUE_B)
        law_label = Text("Physical Law", font_size=16).next_to(self.grid["E2"], DOWN)
        pred_label = Text("Prediction", font_size=16).next_to(self.grid["E6"], DOWN)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow), Write(law_label), Write(pred_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        
        # Final scale to emphasize importance
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.scale(1.1))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Language of Change: An Intuitive Introduction to Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs)
outline.target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school students with basic calculus knowledge

sections.title: The Hook: Capturing Movement
sections.content: Introduce the concept that static numbers cannot describe the world. We need to describe how things change. Define an ODE not as a scary formula, but as a 'rule for growth' or a 'law of motion.'
sections.example: An animation of a Cheetah accelerating. The cheetah's position changes over time, but its velocity (the rate of change of position) also changes based on its current energy and intent. This relationship is an ODE.

sections.title: Prerequisite Bridge: The Slope as a Rate
sections.content: Briefly revisit the derivative (dy/dx). Visually represent it as the 'slope' of a tangent line at a specific point on a curve. This is the fundamental building block: knowing how fast we are going at any single moment.
sections.example: A visual of a mountain climber on a hill. At any point (x), the steepness of the ground (dy/dx) dictates the climber's effort. If we know the steepness everywhere, can we draw the whole mountain?

sections.title: Defining the ODE: The Puzzle
sections.content: Define an ODE as an equation involving a function and its derivatives. Unlike algebraic equations (find x), in ODEs we 'find the function y(x)'. Explain that the equation tells us how the function's value and its slope are locked together.
sections.example: Mathematical notation: dy/dx = y. Graphically, this means 'The steeper the hill gets, the higher up I am.' Animation shows a curve growing steeper as it rises.

sections.title: Visualizing Solutions: Slope Fields
sections.content: Introduce 'Slope Fields' (Vector Fields) as a way to see the solution before solving it. Every point in space has a tiny arrow indicating the required slope. The solution is a path that 'follows the arrows.'
sections.example: Imagine a river filled with tiny floating arrows pointing in different directions. If you drop a paper boat (the starting condition) into the water, the path the boat takes is the solution to the ODE.

sections.title: Application: The Rabbit Colony Growth
sections.content: Apply the concept to population dynamics (The Malthusian Model). The rate of change of the population (dP/dt) is proportional to the current population (P). The more rabbits there are, the faster they multiply.
sections.example: An animation starts with 2 rabbits. The ODE dP/dt = kP is shown. As the number of rabbits on screen increases, the 'speed' of new rabbits appearing increases, resulting in an exponential curve.

sections.title: General vs. Particular Solutions
sections.content: Explain that an ODE has many possible solutions (General Solution) until we define a starting point (Initial Condition), which gives us the one true path (Particular Solution).
sections.example: A 'Family of Curves' animation. Multiple parallel exponential paths are shown (the General Solution). A 'Start' button is clicked at a specific coordinate (0, 5), and one specific path highlights in gold (the Particular Solution).

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Scope
sections.content: Wrap up by emphasizing that ODEs govern everything from satellite orbits to the cooling of a cup of coffee. They are the bridge between a physical law and predicting the future.
sections.example: A split-screen montage showing a swinging pendulum, a circuit board, and a cooling cake, with their corresponding ODEs appearing briefly over them as they move/change.

storyboard.title: The Hook: Capturing Movement
lecture_lines: Numbers alone cannot describe a world in motion.
We need a way to capture how things change.
Differential equations are rules for this growth.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Bridge: The Slope as a Rate
lecture_lines: The derivative represents the slope at a point.
It tells us our instantaneous rate of change.
Knowing every slope allows us to reconstruct paths.
animations: Draw a smooth hill curve and place a small climber dot on it. [Color: #888888]
Animate a tangent line following the dot as it moves, highlighting the slope dy/dx. [Color: #FF00FF]
Show a numerical value for the slope updating in real-time as the dot moves. [Color: #FFFFFF]

storyboard.title: Defining the ODE: The Puzzle
lecture_lines: An ODE relates a function to its derivatives.
We solve for functions, not just single numbers.
This equation locks the value and slope together.
For example, growth increases as the value rises.
The function's behavior depends on its current state.
animations: Center the equation dy/dx = y using large text. [Color: #00FFFF]
Highlight the 'y' variable with a pulsating glow to emphasize it as a function. [Color: #FFFF00]
Render a small tangent segment at a point (x,y) where its slope equals y. [Color: #00FF00]
Transition the segment into a series of segments across the grid. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Draw the function y = e^x and show that it satisfies the slope condition at every point. [Color: #FFA500]

storyboard.title: Visualizing Solutions: Slope Fields
lecture_lines: We can visualize solutions using a slope field.
Every point shows a tiny arrow of direction.
These arrows map the required slope everywhere.
A solution is a path following these arrows.
Like a boat drifting along a river's current.
animations: Display a grid of short, uniform arrows whose slopes are determined by an ODE. [Color: #555555]

Trace a single solution curve that moves through the grid, tangent to the arrows, with a boat [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/boat.svg] traveling along the path. [Color: #0000FF]
Fade in several other solution curves starting from different initial points. [Color: #FFFFFF]

storyboard.title: Application: The Rabbit Colony Growth
lecture_lines: Consider a growing population of rabbits.
The growth rate depends on the current population.
More rabbits lead to faster reproduction.
This relationship creates a specific growth curve.
We call this model exponential growth.
animations: Show a few rabbit icons [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rabbit.svg] at the origin of a coordinate system. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Write the equation dP/dt = kP at the top of the frame. [Color: #00FFFF]
Animate the rabbit icons [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rabbit.svg] duplicating exponentially over time. [Color: #FFC0CB]
Plot the graph of P(t) = P0 * e^(kt) simultaneously with the population growth. [Color: #00FF00]
Use a flashing effect to show the relationship between population size and growth rate. [Color: #FFFF00]

storyboard.title: General vs. Particular Solutions
lecture_lines: One equation can have many possible solutions.
An initial condition picks one unique path.
This specific path is the particular solution.
animations: Plot a family of curves y = e^x + C for various values of C. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Label the set of curves as the 'General Solution.' [Color: #FFFFFF]
Highlight a specific point (0, 2) on the graph with a red dot. [Color: #FF0000]
Fade out all curves except the one that passes through (0, 2). [Color: #FFD700]
Bold the equation for the remaining curve as the 'Particular Solution.' [Color: #FFD700]

Master this language to understand the world.

issues.description:
[section_3] Create Manim code for Defining the ODE.
Script: 1. An ODE like dy/dx = y relates a function to its derivative. 2. Here, 'y' is the unknown function we seek. 3. It tells us the slope depends on the current value. 4. We can visualize these slopes as segments in a grid. 5. Solving it reveals a curve, like y = e^x.
Animation: 1. Display equation dy/dx = y. 2. Highlight 'y' and label as 'unknown function'. 3. Show a single slope segment at a point. 4. Populate a grid with these segments (vector field style). 5. Trace the curve y = e^x through the grid.
Make the transition from formula to grid visualization clear.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented the animation sequence: equation dy/dx=y, highlighting 'y' as the unknown function, showing a specific slope segment, transitioning to a vector field, and overlaying the solution curve y=e^x. Used the grid system for all placements.

issues.description:
[section_4] Create Manim code for Slope Fields.
Script: 1. This grid is called a 'Slope Field'. 2. Picking a starting point traces a unique path. 3. Different starts lead to a whole family of curves.
Animation: 1. Show a dense grid of small arrows/segments for dy/dx = y. 2. Animate a point moving through the field, leaving a trail. 3. Show multiple paths appearing from different starting y-values.
Focus on the 'flow' of the arrows guiding the curves.
issues.resolution_note: Created slope field for dy/dx = y/2, animated a point (boat) following the field to form a blue curve, and displayed a family of white curves starting from different points. Corrected colors and grid positioning applied.

issues.description:
[section_5] Create Manim code for the Rabbit Colony Growth.
Script: 1. A colony of rabbits grows proportional to its size. 2. We write this as dP/dt = kP. 3. More rabbits mean even faster growth. 4. The population curve shoots upward exponentially. 5. This ODE models the 'Language of Change' in biology.
Animation: 1. Start with a few rabbit icons. 2. Display dP/dt = kP. 3. Icons multiply rapidly across the screen. 4. Plot an exponential graph (P vs t). 5. Link the slope of the graph to the growth rate.
Use clean icons and a clear coordinate system for the graph.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented the Rabbit Colony Growth animation. Features include: Coordinate system with population labels, initial dots for rabbits, a multiplication effect representing exponential growth, the ODE dP/dt = kP, an exponential graph P(t), and a flashing effect linking the population size to the curve. Used the 6x6 grid system for all layout components.

issues.description:
[section_6] Create Manim code for General vs. Particular Solutions.
Script: 1. Without a starting point, we have a family of curves. 2. This is the 'General Solution'. 3. Fixing an 'Initial Condition', like (0, 2), picks one. 4. It isolates a single specific curve. 5. This is the 'Particular Solution'.
Animation: 1. Show multiple exponential curves (family). 2. Label the set as 'General Solution'. 3. Highlight the point (0, 2) on the y-axis. 4. Fade out all curves except the one passing through (0, 2). 5. Label the remaining curve 'Particular Solution'.
The contrast between many curves and one curve should be visually distinct.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented the family of curves y=e^x + C, highlighting the point (0, 2) and isolating the particular solution curve y=e^x + 1 with the specified colors and labels.

issues.description:
[section_7] Create Manim code for the Summary.
Script: 1. ODEs describe pendulums, circuits, and cooling cups. 2. They are the universal language of change. 3. Welcome to the world of differential equations.
Animation: 1. Show small icons/animations of a pendulum, a circuit diagram, and a steaming coffee cup. 2. Overlay a unique ODE on each. 3. Fade icons to the final title: 'The Language of Change: ODEs'.
Keep the ending professional and visually cohesive.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented summary scene with pendulum, circuit, and cooling cup animations. Added ODE overlays and final title card.
